_what: Step 1 of the IPD execution plan: an ADMISSIBILITY scan of the reachable EMC survival series. It asks what the published TEXT reports, and deliberately digitises nothing.
_why: emc_ipd_survival.py refuses any curve without a numbers-at-risk table (Guyot's hard conditional: without one, the 97.5% bound admits an error factor of exp(1.556)=4.7 on the hazard ratio). Whether these papers carry one decides whether the route has any admissible input at all.
_not_medical_advice: Nothing here is medical advice, and nothing here asserts efficacy, safety or clinical readiness.

_retrieval.route: workflow_dispatch of .github/workflows/fetch-literature.yml with an inline targets_json manifest of Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoints

⛔_the_headline_is_a_LIMIT_OF_THE_METHOD_: ZERO of the five retrieved papers mentions numbers at risk in its TEXT, and zero prints them in a <table-wrap>. THIS MUST NOT BE REPORTED AS 'no EMC series carries a numbers-at-risk table'. In JATS XML the at-risk row is rendered INSIDE THE FIGURE IMAGE, so a full-text search is structurally incapable of seeing it whether or not it is there. CLAUDE.md s4: an absent reading is not a reading of absence. The question is OPEN and is answered by LOOKING at the figure graphics, which this scan deliberately did not do.
⚠_two_of_seven_were_never_retrieved: drilon2008 (PMC2779719) and bishop2019 (PMC7771031) both returned HTTP 404 from the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint. A PMCID exists for each, so this is a statement about THAT ENDPOINT, not about whether the paper has a full text or a survival figure. Retry via a different route before concluding anything about them.
⭐_what_the_scan_DID_establish: Four of the five retrieved papers report Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. chiusole2020 alone prints FOUR overall-survival curves stratified by resection extent, sex, primary location and metastatic site -- the richest single candidate found. stacchiotti2013anthracycline mentions no Kaplan-Meier analysis at all and is the one retrieved paper that probably carries no curve.
_next_step: Inspect the figure graphics for an at-risk row. NOTE the distinction that governs it: asking 'is there a numbers-at-risk row under this axis?' is a BOUNDED YES/NO OBSERVATION and is safe. Reading coordinates off the plotted curve is a hand step whose error nothing in this repository measures, and it remains trimcrae's decision (see the memo s5.3).

step_1b_figure_route_probe._what: Step 1b: find a route to the Kaplan-Meier figure graphics, where a numbers-at-risk row lives if it exists, and establish whether the question is answerable from text at all.
step_1b_figure_route_probe._answer: IT IS NOT. The chiusole2020 figures are RASTER IMAGES. Settled by a discriminating observation rather than assumed: the PDF text layer carries the figure CAPTIONS (typeset page text) but ZERO plot internals -- no axis tick labels, no '0.0/0.2/.../1.0' survival-axis tokens, no bare numeric rows. So the absence of 'at risk' from both the XML and the PDF text is UNINFORMATIVE in exactly the way s4 warns, and the admissibility question can only be closed by LOOKING at the graphic.

⭐_two_papers_definitively_closed.finding: drilon2008 (PMC2779719) and bishop2019 (PMC7771031) both return error code 'idIsNotOpenAccess' from the OA service. Their earlier HTTP 404 on fullTextXML was NOT an endpoint quirk -- these papers are not open access, and no open route will reach them.
⭐_two_papers_definitively_closed.consequence: They stay on the candidate list with full_text_reachable resolved to False. Reaching them needs a subscription or an interlibrary route, which is trimcrae's to decide, not a free step.

⭐_printed_numbers_recovered_from_chiusol._what: Safe transcription from the PDF text layer -- no digitisation. These are exactly what a printed-numbers-only paper (memo s5.3 option 3) would rest on, and they are already in hand.
⭐_printed_numbers_recovered_from_chiusol.⚠: Transcribed from the extracted text layer, not read off a figure. Each should be checked against the published table before use in any manuscript.
